fr.elements: Main Residence; Solar Panel System; Walkway; Vehicle Parking Area; Landscaped Area; Landscaped Area; Access Drive
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow fire apparatus and emergency vehicles to reach the residence without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive so that a full-width vehicle lane remains open and visible.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the main residence to open a clear path around the structure for responders on foot.
• Remove or thin dense vegetation between structures so responders can move between buildings without obstruction.
• Mark a designated turnaround area at or near the end of the access drive so arriving apparatus crews can identify it immediately.
• Keep the turnaround area free of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials at all times.
• Post visible signage or markings near the structures identifying the number of buildings on the property so arriving crews can account for all structures quickly.
• Notify your local fire department of the single access point and limited turnaround so crews can pre-plan an approach before an emergency occurs.
• Provide the location of the solar panel system and its shutoff point to your local fire department for pre-incident planning.
• Mark or label the solar panel system shutoff in a location visible to arriving responders.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from large trees that overhang or touch the house or roof.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure so trees are not touching each other.
• Remove low-hanging branches from scattered trees close to the house, starting from the ground up.
• Cut back shrubs and plants growing directly against the foundation or exterior walls.
• Keep the area directly around the house clear of leaf litter, fallen branches, and dead plant material dropped by nearby trees.
• Maintain open ground between the base of trees and any shrubs growing beneath them so fire cannot climb from low plants up into the tree canopy.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and debris so vehicles can move through without obstruction.
